summary: Donald S. Lopez Jr. is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his BA and PhD at the University of Virginia, studying under Jeffrey Hopkins, and held professorships at Middlebury College (1986) and the University of Michigan (1990).

Donald Wiebe is a scholar in religious studies and philosophy. He served on the faculty at Trinity College, Toronto, from approximately 1980 to 2018 and was General Editor of Toronto Studies in Religion (attested 1996).
Dondub Buddhayin was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He served as abbot of Chilttai Monastery and of Ganden Dargye Ling (attested 1933), and he taught Eugène Obermiller.

id: P:Dong Kam Tulku Ngawang Damchö Gyatso
summary: Dong Kam Tulku Ngawang Damchö Gyatso studied under Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye.
Dongak Chokyi Nyima studied under Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye.

Dongak Tendzin studied under Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo. He also taught Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, and Shechen Gyaltsab.

Dongchu (1908–1977) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Minnan Buddhist Institute and under Taixu, Aiting, and Nanting. He served as dean at Jiaoshan Buddhist Academy (~1938–1945) and abbot of Dinghui Monastery (~1945–1949).

Donna C. Kurtz is an archaeology and history scholar who studied at the University of Cincinnati, Yale University, and Somerville College. She held a post at the Classical Art Research Centre from approximately 1970 to 2011.

Dor Bahadur Bista is a scholar in Tibetology who studied at Tri-Chandra Multiple Campus (~1950–1954). He served as a professor at Tribhuvan University (~1976–1993) and on the board of governors of ICIMOD.
Doranne Jacobson is an Indologist who completed a doctorate in anthropology at Columbia University, where she also served as a seminar associate at the Southern Asian Institute.

Doris Meth Srinivasan is a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. She earned her PhD from the University of Pennsylvania, served as a curator at the Nelson-Atkins Museum of Art (~2001–2006), and held research posts at Stony Brook University.
Doris Unterthurner is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned her MA at the University of Vienna under the supervision of Klaus-Dieter Mathes.

Dorje Rinchen (1819–1867) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under several teachers, including Sakya Yab Jé Kün Ga Rinchen and Chime Tenpai Nyima, and he taught Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.

Dorje Tseten (1925–2013) was a scholar in Tibetology, history, and archaeology. He earned a degree in education from Beijing Normal University (~1944–1948) and served as director of the China Tibetology Research Center from 1986 to 2000.

Dorji Banzarov (1822–1855) worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, religious studies, and linguistics. He attended the First Kazan Male Gymnasium and completed his doctoral dissertation at Kazan State University (~1842–1846) under Józef Szczepan Kowalewski.

Dorji Wangchuk is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at Ngagyur Nyingma Institute and the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen and David P. Jackson, becoming a professor at the University of Hamburg in 2009.

Dorothy C. Wong is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. She was a visiting Professor of Buddhist Art at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2009) and is affiliated with the University of Virginia (attested 2026).

Douglas Allen is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies who earned degrees from Yale and Vanderbilt. He taught at Southern Illinois University and Central Connecticut State University before serving as professor at the University of Maine from 1981.
Douglas Gildow is a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. He completed his PhD at Princeton University under the supervision of Stephen F. Teiser and Qi Zhou.
Douglas J. Penick is an author and scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Princeton University from ~1962 to 1966 and under the traditional teacher Chögyam Trungpa in 1971.
